title: 421. Hating yourself will get you nowhere

sentences.en: This is an iHeart Podcast, Guaranteed Human.
sentences.zh: 这是一个iHeart播客，保证由人类制作。

sentences.en: I've been really trying to prioritize my health in a realistic way this year, and something that has kept me really motivated is my WHOOP.
sentences.zh: 今年我一直在努力以一种现实的方式优先考虑我的健康，而让我保持动力的东西就是我的WHOOP。

sentences.en: I am such a data person, which is why I love WHOOP, because I can genuinely see why my body feels differently depending on the day, why I'm running differently,
sentences.zh: 我是一个非常看重数据的人，这就是我喜欢WHOOP的原因，因为我可以真正看出为什么我的身体在不同日子里会有不同的感觉，为什么我跑步的状态不同，

sentences.en: why I'm maybe less focused.
sentences.zh: 为什么我有时注意力不集中。

sentences.en: WHOOP effortlessly tracks my sleep, it tracks my strain, my recovery, my stress, and most importantly, my overall health.
sentences.zh: WHOOP可以轻松追踪我的睡眠、身体压力、恢复情况、压力水平，最重要的是，我的整体健康状况。

sentences.en: And it just gives me all that data and all those patterns so I can make better decisions, which includes knowing when to go easy and knowing when to go hard.
sentences.zh: 它为我提供了所有这些数据和模式，让我能够做出更好的决策，包括知道什么时候该放松，什么时候该努力。

sentences.zh: 新用户可以在加入会员之前，通过30天免费试用体验WHOOP。

sentences.en: That's join.whoop.com slash psychology for your free month of WHOOP.
sentences.zh: 访问join.whoop.com/psychology即可免费获得一个月的WHOOP体验。

sentences.zh: 你有什么绝对不会扔掉的珍贵物品吗？

sentences.en: A movie ticket, a boarding pass, or maybe something that makes no sense to anyone but you.
sentences.zh: 一张电影票、一张登机牌，或者其他对别人来说毫无意义，但对你却意义非凡的东西。

sentences.zh: 在新的播客节目《Charmed with Sam Todd》中，

sentences.en: Sam explores the memories, obsessions, and tiny treasures that become part of who you are.
sentences.zh: Sam探索了那些成为你生命一部分的记忆、执念和微小的珍宝。

sentences.en: Charmed is warm, it's funny, it's nostalgic, and just full of the little moments and memories that make life matter.
sentences.zh: 《Charmed》温暖、幽默、充满怀旧感，满载着那些让生活变得有意义的点滴瞬间和记忆。

sentences.en: Charmed with Sam Todd.
sentences.zh: 很高兴认识萨姆·托德。

sentences.en: Stories worn to tell with Pandora.
sentences.zh: Pandora为你讲述那些值得铭记的故事。

sentences.en: Listen now on iHeart.
sentences.zh: 现在就在iHeart上收听吧。

sentences.en: Hello everybody, I'm Gemma Spake, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through the biggest changes, moments, and transitions of our 20s,
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是Gemma Spake，欢迎回到《The Psychology of Your 20s》，在这个播客里，我们探讨20多岁时经历的最大变化、时刻和转型，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello everybody, welcome back to the show, welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到节目，欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: It is so great to have you here, back for another episode.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你们能回来，继续收听新的一期节目。

sentences.en: Not much chit-chat this morning, guys, not much small talk, because we have a big episode.
sentences.zh: 今天早上就不多闲聊了，伙计们，因为我们要聊一个重磅话题。

sentences.en: A big episode on something that I have been thinking about a lot recently, which is how normalized it has become to actively hate yourself, and how almost hated you are
sentences.zh: 这是一个我最近思考了很多的话题，那就是“积极地自我厌恶”变得多么常态化，以及如果你说出或表现出你爱自己，

sentences.en: online, in person, in the real world, if you say or show that you love yourself.
sentences.zh: 你在网上、现实生活中、在真实世界里会受到多么大的排斥。

sentences.en: How in the world did we get here?
sentences.zh: 我们到底是怎么走到这一步的？

sentences.en: Why does that make any sense?
sentences.zh: 为什么这会变得合情合理？

sentences.en: And to perhaps get a little bit conspiratorial on you all, who is benefiting from this?
sentences.zh: 而且，也许要对大家说点阴谋论的话，谁从中受益了呢？

sentences.en: Who is benefiting from this system of self-loathing?
sentences.zh: 谁从这种自我厌恶的体系中获益了？

sentences.en: Who set this all up so that self-hatred is the status quo and self-love is the thing that is seen as sinful or bad?
sentences.zh: 是谁设定了这一切，让自我厌恶成了现状，而自我关爱却被视为罪恶或错误？

sentences.en: It just seems to me a little bit ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这简直有点荒谬。

sentences.en: And I also personally think it's keeping a lot of us stuck in places that we don't want to be.
sentences.zh: 而且我个人认为，这让很多人困在了他们不想待的地方。

sentences.en: I've been saying this so much on the podcast recently, in so many different episodes, you can't hate yourself into a successful life.
sentences.zh: 我最近在播客里反复提到这一点，在很多不同的节目里都说过：你不可能通过自我厌恶来获得成功的人生。

sentences.en: And I thought, you know, there's only so many times I can say that before I just do a full freaking episode on it.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，我说了这么多遍，是时候专门做一期完整的节目来聊聊它了。

sentences.en: And today is that day.
sentences.zh: 今天就是这一天。

sentences.en: We're going to look at the science and the psychology that proves you cannot hate yourself into a successful life.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨科学和心理学，证明你无法通过自我厌恶来实现成功的人生。

sentences.en: And yeah, essentially just dissects where your self-hatred comes from and why it's lying to you.
sentences.zh: 是的，本质上就是剖析你的自我厌恶从何而来，以及它为什么在欺骗你。

sentences.en: You know, it's not going to make you humble.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它不会让你变得谦逊。

sentences.en: It's not going to make you more successful because of that humility.
sentences.zh: 它也不会因为那种谦逊而让你变得更成功。

sentences.en: You cannot bully yourself into being better.
sentences.zh: 你无法通过霸凌自己来让自己变得更好。

sentences.en: Even if it gets momentary results, it is not a long-term motivational force the way that we tend to think it will be.
sentences.zh: 即使它能带来暂时的结果，它也不是我们通常认为的那种长期动力。

sentences.en: This is a big episode today.
sentences.zh: 今天这期节目很重要。

sentences.en: We have a lot to explore.
sentences.zh: 我们有很多内容要探索。

sentences.en: I really particularly want to drill into the origins of this feeling and of this like psychological self-loathing.
sentences.zh: 我特别想深入挖掘这种感觉和这种心理上的自我厌恶的根源。

sentences.en: And then also, of course, provide some evidence-based strategies to eliminate that mindset, especially if you are in your 20s, because if there was going to be a time in your life
sentences.zh: 当然，我也会提供一些基于证据的策略来消除这种心态，特别是如果你正处于20多岁，因为如果说你生命中有一个阶段

sentences.en: where you really needed to have a deep sense of self-belief, it would be this time.
sentences.zh: 最需要深刻的自我信念，那就是现在。

sentences.en: It would be right now.
sentences.zh: 就是此时此刻。

sentences.en: So I feel like if you are struggling with self-doubt and self-loathing that has become insidious and is bleeding into everything that you're doing,
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，如果你正在与那种已经变得阴险并渗透到你所做一切事情中的自我怀疑和自我厌恶作斗争，

sentences.en: this is the perfect episode for you.
sentences.zh: 这期节目非常适合你。

sentences.en: Without further ado, let's talk about why hating yourself will get you nowhere you want to be and, of course, the alternative.
sentences.zh: 废话不多说，让我们来谈谈为什么自我厌恶只会让你一事无成，以及当然，还有其他的选择。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: Let's start here.
sentences.zh: 我们从这里开始。

sentences.en: Why does it feel easier to hate ourselves rather than love ourselves?
sentences.zh: 为什么比起爱自己，我们觉得厌恶自己更容易？

sentences.en: Like, instinctually,
sentences.zh: 就像，本能地，

sentences.en: why does it feel easier to dismiss a compliment or to be self-deprecating in front of other people?
sentences.zh: 为什么忽视赞美或在别人面前自嘲感觉更容易？

sentences.en: Or why does it feel easier to focus in on all the things we dislike about our bodies and dislike about our personalities and dislike about our work ethic
sentences.zh: 或者为什么比起关注我们喜欢的特质，我们更容易专注于自己身体、性格和工作态度中那些我们不喜欢的地方？

sentences.en: rather than the things that we like?
sentences.zh: （接上句）而不是我们喜欢的地方？

sentences.en: That doesn't come from nowhere.
sentences.zh: 这并非空穴来风。

sentences.en: And the best evidence that this is an external influence, first and foremost, that becomes internalized, the best evidence for this is being around children, right?
sentences.zh: 最好的证据表明这是一种外部影响，首先被内化了，最好的证据就是观察孩子，对吧？

sentences.en: Being around kids and seeing that before the age of four or five, children have no concept that there is something about themselves that could be unlikable.
sentences.zh: 观察孩子，你会发现四五岁之前，孩子根本没有“自己身上有什么地方是不讨人喜欢的”这种概念。

sentences.en: Like, that is not even something that enters their consciousness.
sentences.zh: 这甚至根本没有进入他们的意识。

sentences.en: They don't even think about it.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至都不会去想。

sentences.en: But then it's almost like there comes a point where a switch gets flipped, a switch gets turned.
sentences.zh: 但后来，似乎到了某个时刻，开关被拨动了，开关被打开了。

sentences.en: My friend, actually, she has two kids, one who is three and one who is eight.
sentences.zh: 其实我的朋友有两个孩子，一个三岁，一个八岁。

sentences.en: I was watching them the other day and we were doing like arts and craft and like the younger one is just like scribbling, she's having fun and like doesn't really care,
sentences.zh: 前几天我看着他们，我们当时在做手工，小的那个就在乱涂乱画，她玩得很开心，根本不在乎，

sentences.en: she's like exploring.
sentences.zh: 她只是在探索。

sentences.en: And the eight-year-old was like, this one isn't good.
sentences.zh: 而那个八岁的孩子却说：“这个不好看。”

sentences.en: Like, this one is bad.
sentences.zh: “这个很糟糕。”

sentences.en: My art is bad.
sentences.zh: “我的画太烂了。”

sentences.en: Like, I have to start over again.
sentences.zh: “我得重画。”

sentences.en: And just like the parallel, like the juxtaposition between these two people was like quite striking.
sentences.zh: 这种对比，这两个人之间的并置，非常引人注目。

sentences.en: So where does this come from?
sentences.zh: 那么这从何而来呢？

sentences.en: When does this self-loathing first hit?
sentences.zh: 这种自我厌恶是什么时候开始出现的？

sentences.en: Psychology will tell us that a lot of self-hatred starts as a form of adaptation.
sentences.zh: 心理学告诉我们，很多自我厌恶始于一种适应形式。

sentences.en: When we're young, we don't yet have like a fully formed, stable sense of self.
sentences.zh: 当我们年轻时，我们还没有形成一个完全稳定、成熟的自我意识。

sentences.en: So we often borrow our reflections and borrow our sense of identity from other people who we spend a lot of time around.
sentences.zh: 所以我们经常从身边的人那里借用我们的投射和身份认同。

sentences.en: Parents, teachers, siblings, peers, they kind of help us build the first draft of how you understand yourself by offering suggestions, but sometimes also offering criticism
sentences.zh: 父母、老师、兄弟姐妹、同龄人，他们通过提供建议，有时也通过提供批评，帮助我们构建了自我认知的初稿，

sentences.en: and also by displaying self-criticism towards themselves.
sentences.zh: 也通过对自己表现出的自我批评（来影响我们）。

sentences.en: This is what we call, this first sense of self is what we call the evaluative self.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们所说的，这种最初的自我感被称为“评价性自我”。

sentences.en: We learn about what it means to be human by seeing what others are doing, thinking about what others are doing, copying other people's behaviors,
sentences.zh: 我们通过观察他人的行为、思考他人的行为、模仿他人的行为来学习做人的意义，

sentences.en: and also comparing our own behavior or our own little lives to what we see around us.
sentences.zh: 同时也通过将我们自己的行为或我们的小生活与周围所见进行比较。

sentences.en: At some point, we become aware that there is an audience.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，我们意识到有一个观众存在。

sentences.en: We're not always performing for the same audience though.
sentences.zh: 不过我们并不总是为同一个观众表演。

sentences.en: We become aware as children there is an audience.
sentences.zh: 作为孩子，我们意识到有一个观众。

sentences.en: Some of our childhood audiences were a lot meaner.
sentences.zh: 我们童年时期的一些观众非常刻薄。

sentences.en: Some of our parents weren't very nice.
sentences.zh: 我们的一些父母并不友善。

sentences.en: Some of our peers weren't very nice.
sentences.zh: 我们的一些同龄人并不友善。

sentences.en: Some of our teachers weren't very nice.
sentences.zh: 我们的一些老师并不友善。

sentences.en: If those early environments are warm, you often learn that mistakes are survivable and that your worth will remain intact even when you get things wrong,
sentences.zh: 如果那些早期的环境是温暖的，你通常会学到错误是可以挽回的，即使你做错了事，你的价值依然完好无损，

sentences.en: even when you're not perfect.
sentences.zh: 即使你并不完美。

sentences.en: You're happy to explore.
sentences.zh: 你乐于探索。

sentences.en: You're happy to bounce back.
sentences.zh: 你乐于反弹。

sentences.en: You're happy to, you just are resilient.
sentences.zh: 你乐于，你只是很有韧性。

sentences.en: Like I think about my friend's kid, right?
sentences.zh: 就像我想起我朋友的孩子，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, she didn't like her art, but just because she didn't like it when it was compared to like the idea of somebody else's picture, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，她不喜欢她的画，但那只是因为当她把它与别人的画作进行比较时，她觉得不好，对吧？

sentences.en: Not because her parents were like screaming at her that she was terrible at everything she does.
sentences.zh: 而不是因为她的父母冲她大喊大叫，说她做什么都一无是处。

sentences.en: Like she didn't like it from a comparative sense.
sentences.zh: 她只是从比较的角度觉得不好。

sentences.en: For some people though,
sentences.zh: 然而对有些人来说，

sentences.en: like their environment, like the inner critic was always external.
sentences.zh: 他们的环境，他们的内心批判者总是外化的。

sentences.en: It was a highly critical, rejecting, humiliating, unpredictable, cruel, completely disengaged person who was like speaking things in their ear, telling them they were terrible.
sentences.zh: 那是一个高度挑剔、排斥、羞辱、不可预测、残忍、完全冷漠的人，在他们耳边低语，告诉他们他们很糟糕。

sentences.en: Children are watching so closely.
sentences.zh: 孩子们观察得非常仔细。

sentences.en: They are listening so closely and they internalize the tone of our own language, not just towards them, but towards ourselves as well.
sentences.zh: 他们听得非常仔细，并内化了我们语言的基调，不仅是对他们，也是对我们自己。

sentences.en: Research has consistently found that higher self-criticism and self-hatred as an adult.
sentences.zh: 研究一致发现，成年后的高自我批评和自我厌恶，

sentences.en: If you have more of those things as an adult, it's greatly associated with early memories of parental rejection or conditional affection from parents, but also from favoritism,
sentences.zh: 如果你成年后有更多这些特质，它与童年时期父母的排斥或有条件的爱有很大关联，也与偏袒有关，

sentences.en: from favoritism, from teachers, from childhood bullying, basically just harmful experiences that occurred right as we were forming our evaluative self.
sentences.zh: 来自老师的偏袒、童年霸凌，基本上就是发生在我们构建评价性自我时期的有害经历。

sentences.en: For example, there was a 2006 study published in the Journal of Affective Disorders and it looked at the impact of childhood verbal abuse on how adults view themselves.
sentences.zh: 例如，2006年发表在《情感障碍杂志》上的一项研究观察了童年言语虐待对成年人自我认知的影响。

sentences.en: They analyzed the data of like 6,000 people and they found that heavy or high levels of criticism and discipline and like non-purposeful discipline, experiencing that as a child,
sentences.zh: 他们分析了约6000人的数据，发现童年时期经历过高水平的批评、管教以及无目的的管教，

sentences.en: has a really significant impact on the development of things like adult depression and adult anxiety.
sentences.zh: 对成年后抑郁和焦虑的发展有显著影响。

sentences.en: The researchers described the role of self-criticism in these studies as basically a full mediator.
sentences.zh: 研究人员在这些研究中将自我批评的作用描述为一种完全的中介因素。

sentences.en: So this basically means that the verbal abuse didn't directly cause the depression, but it causes a child to develop a self-critical brain because of course
sentences.zh: 这意味着言语虐待并没有直接导致抑郁，但它导致孩子发展出了一个自我批评的大脑，因为当然，

sentences.en: they're going to believe what an adult says about them.
sentences.zh: 他们会相信成年人对他们的评价。

sentences.en: They're the role model.
sentences.zh: 他们是榜样。

sentences.en: They're the adult.
sentences.zh: 他们是成年人。

sentences.en: And that self-critical brain is what drives some parts or a lot of parts of adult depression.
sentences.zh: 而那个自我批评的大脑正是驱动成年后抑郁症部分或大部分原因的因素。

sentences.en: A similar story is definitely seen in terms of peer experiences as well.
sentences.zh: 在同伴经历方面，情况也绝对类似。

sentences.en: When we're kids, when we are teenagers, this weird social like pecking order can emerge as people kind of like fight to promote their evaluative selves
sentences.zh: 当我们还是孩子、青少年时，这种奇怪的社会等级制度就会出现，因为人们在争夺提升自己的评价性自我，

sentences.en: and to feel good about themselves.
sentences.zh: 并以此来感觉良好。

sentences.en: Like the main way that we feel good about ourselves as children and teenagers
sentences.zh: 作为孩子和青少年，我们感觉良好的主要方式，

sentences.en: is in reference to other people.
sentences.zh: 是参照他人。

sentences.en: And so to feel better, we often have to result to criticizing others, bullying, making remarks, jokes, feeling a sense of superiority, that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 所以为了感觉更好，我们经常不得不诉诸于批评他人、霸凌、发表评论、开玩笑、产生优越感等等。

sentences.en: Of course, that's not always the case, but it's very, very prevalent.
sentences.zh: 当然，情况并非总是如此，但这非常非常普遍。

sentences.en: And that definitely reinforces the self-hatred of the person being targeted for sure.
sentences.zh: 这绝对强化了被针对者的自我厌恶，这是肯定的。

sentences.en: It also reinforces the self-hatred of the person doing the targeting.
sentences.zh: 它也强化了施加针对行为者的自我厌恶。

sentences.en: Like there is a reason that as teenagers when we are insecure, we feel the need to diminish somebody else.
sentences.zh: 就像青少年时期我们感到不安时，我们觉得有必要贬低别人是有原因的。

sentences.en: And it means that like every person in this situation feels terrible.
sentences.zh: 这意味着在这种情况下，每个人都感觉很糟糕。

sentences.en: This is why self-hatred can feel so intimate because it starts so, so young.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么自我厌恶会让人感觉如此亲密，因为它开始得太早了。

sentences.en: Someone else's voice when heard enough times with enough authority or emotional force can stick with us and form part of who we think we are.
sentences.zh: 当别人的声音被听到足够多次，且带有足够的权威或情感力量时，它就会扎根于我们心中，成为我们自我认知的一部分。

sentences.en: Eventually, like if this criticism becomes loud enough, it no longer needs somebody else to be present.
sentences.zh: 最终，如果这种批评变得足够响亮，它就不再需要别人的存在了。

sentences.en: Like we inherently believe that yes, we aren't that talented.
sentences.zh: 我们从内心深处相信，是的，我们确实没那么有才华。

sentences.en: Yes, we aren't that attractive.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们确实没那么有吸引力。

sentences.en: Yes, we aren't that smart.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们确实没那么聪明。

sentences.en: Yes, we aren't somebody that others want to be around because we're hearing it from maybe a parent.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们确实不是别人想与之相处的人，因为我们可能从父母那里听到了这些话。
